text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

An all-male panel is worth noticing when it may have disadvantaged someone — but you and the successful candidate are both men. The panel's composition cannot explain why he was chosen over you. Raising it would signal you're searching for a grievance rather than engaging with the actual decision, and would weaken any legitimate point you make.

Your stronger ground is substantive: you hold a master's and a professional licence against his bachelor's, and twelve years of municipal planning against an unspecified consultation background. That raises a fair question about whether the stated criteria were applied as advertised.

Focus on the unanswered request. Send a follow-up citing your original date, and ask whether your municipality's recruitment policy or local records rules set a response deadline.
